sections.h2: Which Oldham County office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
Oldham County's sheriff mails and collects the bill. Its valuation comes from the Property Valuation Administration (PVA). Per the sheriff's tax collection page, a single bill rolls together money owed to the state, the county, school districts, Crestwood and 18 special districts. Envelopes are out by the end of September, and the sheriff can be reached at 502-222-9501.

The sheriff's site also carries a Property Tax FAQ for owners who want more detail on payment options. A value that looks wrong is a PVA matter, at 502-222-9320, because the sheriff never assigns value to any parcel. Each bill spells out when payment is due, how penalties are avoided and what a mortgage servicer's payment looks like.

sections.h2: Why does Oldham County stand out in Kentucky?
sections.html:
Oldham County lies in north central Kentucky as part of metropolitan Louisville. Wikipedia's county profile ranks it first in the state for both wealth and education. Its 196 square miles make it the 13th smallest county in Kentucky, with the Ohio River marking the northern line against Indiana.

Kentucky lawmakers formed it in 1823, using land from Henry, Jefferson and Shelby counties. Towns sprouted along the Louisville and Frankfort railroad during the 1850s, and Interstate 71, completed in the early 1970s, tied the county to downtown Louisville. La Grange is both the seat and the biggest city. Crestwood, Goshen, Pewee Valley, Prospect, Orchard Grass Hills and River Bluff are cities too, and Buckner and Westport are census-designated places. Prospect lies mostly in Jefferson County, so check which county bills a Prospect parcel. Jefferson, Shelby, Henry and Trimble counties adjoin Oldham in Kentucky, with Clark County across the river in Indiana.

Growth shows in the head count: 14,687 people in 1970, 27,795 in 1980, 43,455 in 1990, 60,316 in 2010 and 67,607 in 2020. Students attend Oldham County Schools, which operates North Oldham High School, Oldham County High School and South Oldham High School, and one of the first questions buyers ask is which of the three serves an address.

sections.html:
Prices here run well beyond the Kentucky norm. The table's survey figures span 2020 to 2024.

An owner with a mortgage pays $2,193 a month at the median, against $712 without one. Poverty affects 6.0 percent of residents. The 23,025 households average 2.84 people, and seniors make up 17.1 percent of the population. In the 2020 census, 42.4 percent of households had children under 18 and the median age was 40.0.

sections.h2: When are Oldham County owners expected to pay?
sections.html:
Oldham County follows the statewide calendar in KRS 134.015. Pay by November 1 to save 2 percent, pay the printed amount through December, and expect a 5 percent penalty in January that becomes 10 percent afterward.

  • With escrow, verify the lender paid ahead of the discount deadline.
  • For a fall closing, get the title agent to say who pays the current bill.
  • In Crestwood, the city levy shows up on the sheriff's bill.

The owner on January 1 owes that year's tax, so a spring seller still gets the bill and splits it with the buyer at the closing table.

sections.h2: What can an Oldham County owner do about a high valuation?
sections.html:
The opening step, as a statewide PVA appeal guide describes it, is a PVA conference. Bring your own number and backing for it, such as nearby sales, a recent appraisal, contractor quotes or rent records.

If talks fail, the path leads through the Oldham County Clerk to a three-resident local board and finally to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, where the deadline is 30 days from the mailed ruling. At a $393,100 median, sales from the same subdivision make the strongest evidence.

sections.h2: Where do unpaid Oldham County bills end up?
sections.html:
Anything the sheriff has not collected by closing time on April 15 is handed to the County Clerk. The Oldham County Clerk's delinquent tax page refers value disputes to the PVA and sale questions to the Department of Revenue.

Under the state collection guide, the parcel is liened, interest runs at 1 percent monthly, the county attorney mails warnings, and any sale waits at least 90 days after the transfer. When an investor buys the certificate, the owner then owes the investor. If you are selling, get the clerk's quote and settle it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Which charges land on an Oldham County seller at closing?
sections.html:
Kentucky's transfer tax is the seller's: fifty cents for each $500 of value, counting any remainder as a full $500, taken by the clerk with the deed (KRS 142.050). A $393,100 sale spans 787 units of $500 and owes $393.50. Spouse-to-spouse deeds, corrective deeds and foreclosure deeds are exempt.

  • Every deed lists the full price, mailing addresses for both sides and a forwarding address for the next tax bill.
  • A gift or token-price sale needs a sworn market-value estimate.
  • Heirs file the personal representative's affidavit wherever the estate holds land.

sections.h2: Who are Oldham County's neighbors and likely buyers?
sections.html:
The county packs in more people per acre than most of Kentucky. In 2010 the county averaged 322.2 people per square mile, and by 2020 it averaged 361.1. Veterans number 3,634. High school graduates account for 94.5 percent of adults, 4.2 percent of residents were born outside the United States, and 6.0 percent speak another language at home.

Most households stay put, with 88.4 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier. Just 4.3 percent of people under 65 have no health insurance, and 7.3 percent have a disability. Children make up 23.9 percent of residents, which is why school zones dominate buyer questions.

sections.h2: What is driving the Oldham County housing market?
sections.html:
Growth is steady. The county gained roughly 3,400 residents between April 2020 and July 2025, and builders took out 276 permits in 2025. Bachelor's degrees belong to 46.4 percent of adults, broadband reaches 95.4 percent of households, and a commute averages 26.2 minutes one way.

The jobs picture explains the pull: the county had 1,404 employer establishments and 14,369 jobs in 2023, with $775.1 million in payroll, and employment rose 6.2 percent from 2022 to 2023. A further 6,086 nonemployer businesses operated in 2024, and 64.1 percent of residents aged 16 or older are in the labor force. Retail sales hit $728.0 million in 2022. Health care and social assistance brought in $350.7 million. Wikipedia reports that 74.8 percent of residents lived in urban areas in 2020. The sheriff bills 18 special districts and one city, so neighbors a few miles apart can owe different totals. Check the districts on a bill before comparing listings.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about an Oldham County valuation?
faqs.a: The PVA, 502-222-9320. Values come from that office, and the sheriff only collects what they produce.

faqs.q: When do Oldham County property tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: The sheriff's tax page says mailing wraps up by the end of September. Call 502-222-9501 if yours is missing in early October.

faqs.q: Is Crestwood's city tax billed separately?
faqs.a: No. The Crestwood levy rides on the same sheriff bill as the county and district charges, so a single payment covers all of them.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies to a median-priced Oldham County sale?
faqs.a: $393.50 on a $393,100 sale, owed by the seller and paid to the clerk before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can a house with a tax lien on it still be sold in Oldham County?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk quotes a payoff valid through a stated date, and the title company pays it from the sale proceeds.
